candidate.answerReason: Equal prices make all the CDs cost three times the stated one-third purchase, or 3/5 of her money. She has 2/5 left, matching choice C.

methods.label: Scale the cost of one third of the CDs
methods.explanation:
Because the CDs all have the same price, three groups containing the same number of CDs have the same cost. One third of the CDs costs \(\frac15\) of Brianna's money, so all three thirds cost
\[
3\cdot\frac15=\frac35
\]
of her money. The fraction left is therefore
\[
1-\frac35=\boxed{\frac25},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses equal-price proportional reasoning, multiplication of a fraction by an integer, and a fractional complement.

candidate.annotationRationale: The route-neutral target is direct proportionality between CD count and total cost at a fixed price. review.mathematicalCheck: Equal prices make each third of the CDs cost the same amount. Thus all CDs cost 3·(1/5)=3/5 of her original money, leaving 1−3/5=2/5.
review.levelCheck: Equal-group scaling supplies a complete elementary explanation without requiring a fraction-division equation.
